requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray of at least four cells
requirements.evidence: Build has 4 contiguous hex cells: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full - forming a compact tray. Check_build is clear with joints locked and open faces capped.

requirements.requirement: Each cell with a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Each cell holds a Bin, full depth, drained (hex-bin-full-drain): bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full-drain. All bins have drainage holes for seed-starting.

finish.summary: Built a 4-cell hexagonal tray where every cell contains a full-depth drained bin. Cells are locked together with joint bolts and all perimeter faces capped. Each bin filled with soil and planted with seedling plugs (basil, butterhead lettuce, kale, parsley) to demonstrate seed-starting use. Verified with check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no prop warnings.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
